purpose: Selected final revisions correct the suction arrow and remove ambiguous full-loop piping in favour of a valve close-up

edits.prompt: Edit this refrigerator rear-view educational illustration. Preserve the appliance, lighting, painted 3D style, color palette, all three cream labels, orientation inset, compressor, condenser and outward heat arrows exactly. Make ONLY these two scientifically necessary piping corrections. (1) On the cyan vertical suction tube at the left, REVERSE the upward arrow so it points DOWN, following the tube downward then right INTO the compressor. Keep the other cyan arrows pointing right into the compressor. (2) The amber liquid outlet at the BOTTOM RIGHT of the condenser must NOT connect back into the compressor. Remove its existing horizontal connection into the compressor's right side. Instead route this amber outlet DOWN along the right-hand interior edge of the rear service bay and disappear behind the cabinet at the bottom right, clearly distinct from the compressor. Put a small downward arrow on this outlet. The red hot outlet from the compressor still goes UP into the TOP of the condenser. Exactly the same labels Compressor, Condenser, Heat out; no new words or symbols.

Recompose this illustration into a clearer, scientifically correct CLOSE-UP OF THE EXPANSION VALVE AND COLD RETURN only. Preserve the exquisite soft painted 3D refrigerator style, warm peach-to-blue background, same dark slate cabinet and familiar milk/cabbage/cheese/apples. Remove the compressor, external condenser and all red hot-gas piping completely, so there is no misleading shortcut or T-junction. We are showing only ONE PART of the full circuit here. The right 60 percent shows a cropped three-quarter cutaway of the refrigerator's food compartment and a cyan evaporator coil in its inner left wall. The left 40 percent shows a large elegant magnified view of ONE small brass expansion valve: warm amber liquid pipe enters from the LEFT EDGE, passes through a narrow restriction inside the valve, then becomes a cool cyan mixture exiting to the RIGHT. Thin cyan arrows on the outlet point rightward then up into the BOTTOM of the interior serpentine coil. This cold mixture travels up through the coil, absorbing heat, and a separate blue vapor return exits from the TOP of the coil and leaves toward the back/offscreen, with no connection back into the valve. Orange heat arrows go from the food/air toward the cold coil. Warm inlet and cold outlet are one continuous pipe through the restriction. Three concise cream rounded leader labels exactly: "Expansion valve" at the brass restriction, "Cold return" at the blue outlet immediately AFTER the valve, "Heat absorbed" by the inside coil. No title, no paragraphs, no extra labels, no numeric pressure values, no fans, no open holes in the pipe, no disconnected geometric paths. The macro valve is large enough to show pressure/phase change with fewer larger spaced bubbles in the cold mixture and dense amber liquid before it. This is a close-up explanatory scene, not a whole-system piping diagram.
